stem: Which Sikh Guru was born in Patna?
expl: Guru Gobind Singh was the tenth Guru of the Sikhs. He was born in A.D. 1666 in Patna, Bihar, and died on 7 October, 1708, in Nanded, Maharashtra.

stem: Where was the capital of Shivaji?
expl: In 1674, Shivaji got himself crowned, assumed the title of ‘Chhatrapati’, and made Raigad his capital. The great scholar of that era, Pandit Vishweshwar of Banaras, also known as ‘Ganga Bhatt’, performed his coronation by declaring him a Kshatriya.

stem: 'Ashta Pradhan' was helping in the Administration of which ruler?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: For the administration of the Maratha state, Shivaji created the Ashtapradhan system at the central level, under which eight ministers were appointed. These included Peshwa, Amatya, Mantri, Sachiv, Sumant, Senapati, Panditrao, and Nyayadhish. They functioned like modern-day secretaries in Shivaji’s administration. Their role was only to advise the king. It cannot be called a council of ministers in the real sense. Each minister was responsible to the king. Details are as follows— (i) Peshwa – Prime Minister of the king. (ii) Amatya or Mazumdar – Minister of Finance and Revenue. (iii) Waqia Navis or Mantri – Kept records of the king’s daily work and the day-to-day proceedings of the court. (iv) Sachiv or Shurunavis – Looked after official correspondence. (v) Sumant or Dabir – Foreign Minister. (vi) Senapati or Sar-e-Naubat – Managed recruitment, organization, supplies, etc., of the army. (vii) Panditrao – Responsible for grants to scholars and for religious works. (viii) Nyayadhish – Chief Justice. Official Department a. Sachiva 1. Prime Minister b. Peshwa 2. In-charge of Correspondence c. Sumant 3. Finance Minister d. Amatya 4. Foreign Minister

stem: Who was the last Mughal Emperor to sit on Mayur Singhasan?
expl: The last Mughal ruler to sit on the famous Peacock Throne made by Shah Jahan was Muhammad Shah, because during his reign Nadir Shah invaded India in 1739 and defeated the Mughal army in the Battle of Karnal. Nadir Shah took with him sixty lakh rupees, several thousand ashrafis, gold articles worth one crore rupees, jewels worth fifty crore rupees, the Koh-i-Noor, and the Takht-e-Taus (Peacock Throne) to Iran.

stem: Which of the following Mughal emperors was not allowed to enter into Delhi by Wazir Ghaziuddin?
expl: The reign of Shah Alam II lasted from 1759 to 1806. His real name was Ali Gauhar. At the time of his father Alamgir II’s death, he was in Bihar. Although he was declared the Mughal emperor, due to factionalism in the Mughal court, he remained outside Delhi, and the throne of Delhi remained vacant from 1760 to 1771. In 1772, he could reach Delhi only with the help of the Marathas. During Shah Alam II’s time, the British captured Delhi (1803).
